Package server

Class DBConnector

java.lang.Object
server.DBConnector
public class DBConnector extends Object
The DBConnector class manages the connection to a MySQL database and provides methods to perform various operations related to users, orders, dishes, and restaurants.

This class includes methods for:

  • Connecting to the database
  • Updating order statuses
  • Calculating time differences for orders
  • Managing restaurant and dish data
  • Retrieving reports and statistics

Each method handles a specific database query or update, often wrapping the SQL logic in a way that makes it easier to use in a higher-level application.

This class uses prepared statements to prevent SQL injection attacks. Connections are managed with auto-commit control to ensure database transactions are atomic and reliable.

  • Method Details

    • connectToDB

      public void connectToDB(String dbName, String dbPassword)
      Establishes a connection to the MySQL database using the provided database name and password. The method initializes the connection with the MySQL JDBC driver and handles any exceptions that may occur during the connection process.

      If the connection is successful, a confirmation message is printed to the console. If the connection fails, error messages are printed, detailing the type of failure.

      Parameters:
      dbName - The name of the database to connect to.
      dbPassword - The password for the database user.

    • getUserType

      public String getUserType(String username, String password)
      Retrieves the user type for a given username and password from the database. The method executes a SQL query to fetch the `usertype` associated with the provided credentials. If the credentials match an existing user, the user type is returned. Otherwise, the method returns null.

      If an SQL exception occurs during the query, the exception is caught, and null is returned. The method also prints an error message to the console if no user is found with the provided credentials.

      Parameters:
      username - The username of the user whose type is to be retrieved.
      password - The password associated with the provided username.
      Returns:
      The user type as a String if the user is found, or null if no matching user is found or an exception occurs.

    • updateInPreperation

      public boolean updateInPreperation(int orderId)
      Updates the status of an order to "In Preparation" and sets the current time as the start time. The method executes an SQL `UPDATE` query on the `orders` table, modifying the status and start time for the order identified by the provided order ID. The start time is set to the current system time.

      If the update is successful, the method returns true. If an `SQLException` occurs or no rows are affected, the method returns false and prints the stack trace of the exception.

      Parameters:
      orderId - The ID of the order to be updated.
      Returns:
      true if the order was successfully updated; false otherwise.

    • updateAccept

      public boolean updateAccept(int orderId)
      Updates the status of an order to "Delivered to client" and sets the current time as the end time. The method executes an SQL `UPDATE` query on the `orders` table, modifying the status and end time for the order identified by the provided order ID. The end time is set to the current system time.

      If the update is successful, the method returns true. If an `SQLException` occurs or no rows are affected, the method returns false and prints the stack trace of the exception.

      Parameters:
      orderId - The ID of the order to be updated.
      Returns:
      true if the order was successfully updated; false otherwise.

    • UpdatesCredits

      public boolean UpdatesCredits(int UserId, double credits)
      Updates the credits for a user in the database. The method executes an SQL `UPDATE` query on the `users` table, modifying the `credits` field for the user identified by the provided user ID.

      If the update is successful, the method returns true. If an `SQLException` occurs or no rows are affected, the method returns false and prints the stack trace of the exception.

      Parameters:
      UserId - The ID of the user whose credits need to be updated.
      credits - The new credit amount to be set for the user.
      Returns:
      true if the credits were successfully updated; false otherwise.

    • UpdateLate

      public boolean UpdateLate(int orderId)
      Marks an order as late in the database by setting the `late` field to 1 for the specified order ID. The method executes an SQL `UPDATE` query on the `orders` table, updating the `late` field for the order identified by the provided order ID.

      If the update is successful, the method returns true. If an `SQLException` occurs or no rows are affected, the method returns false and prints the stack trace of the exception.

      Parameters:
      orderId - The ID of the order that needs to be marked as late.
      Returns:
      true if the order was successfully marked as late; false otherwise.

    • updateInDelivery

      public boolean updateInDelivery(int orderId)
      Updates the status of an order to "In Delivery" in the database for the specified order ID. This method executes an SQL `UPDATE` query on the `orders` table, setting the `status` field to "In Delivery" for the order identified by the provided order ID.

      If the update is successful, the method returns true. If an `SQLException` occurs or no rows are affected, the method returns false and prints the stack trace of the exception.

      Parameters:
      orderId - The ID of the order that needs to have its status updated to "In Delivery".
      Returns:
      true if the order status was successfully updated; false otherwise.

    • calculateTimeDifference

      public int calculateTimeDifference(int orderId)
      Calculates the time difference in minutes between the start and end times of an order specified by the given order ID. The method retrieves the start and end times from the database, and then calculates the difference using the calculateDifferenceInMinutes(String, String) method.

      If the start or end time cannot be found, or if an SQL exception occurs, the method returns -1.

      Parameters:
      orderId - The ID of the order for which the time difference is to be calculated.
      Returns:
      The time difference in minutes between the order's start and end times, or -1 if an error occurs or the times are not found.

    • calculateDifferenceInMinutes

      public static int calculateDifferenceInMinutes(String startTime, String endTime)
      Calculates the difference in minutes between two date-time strings formatted as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss".

      This method parses the provided start and end times into LocalDateTime objects using the specified date-time format. It then calculates the difference in minutes between the two date-time values using ChronoUnit.MINUTES.

      Parameters:
      startTime - The start time as a string in the format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss".
      endTime - The end time as a string in the format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss".
      Returns:
      The difference in minutes between the start and end times.
      Throws:
      DateTimeParseException - if the date-time strings cannot be parsed.

    • getActiveOrdersForUser

      public List<Order> getActiveOrdersForUser(int userId)
      Retrieves a list of active orders for a specific user from the database.

      This method fetches orders that have not yet been delivered to the client for a given user. It constructs each order with its details, including the order ID, delivery type, status, and total price. The method groups items by order ID and concatenates dish details with any remarks.

      Parameters:
      userId - The ID of the user whose active orders are to be retrieved.
      Returns:
      A list of Order objects representing the active orders for the specified user. If no active orders are found, an empty list is returned.
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs.

    • placeNewOrder

      public boolean placeNewOrder(int user_id, String address, String phone_num, String email, double total_price, String status, int res_id, String start_time, String end_time, String delivery_type, String req_time, List<Dish> dishes)
      Places a new order in the database and associates the provided dishes with the order.

      This method first inserts the order details into the `orders` table. If the order is successfully inserted, it retrieves the generated order ID and then inserts each dish associated with the order into the `order_items` table.

      Parameters:
      user_id - The ID of the user placing the order.
      address - The delivery address for the order.
      phone_num - The phone number associated with the order.
      email - The email address associated with the order.
      total_price - The total price of the order.
      status - The current status of the order.
      res_id - The ID of the restaurant associated with the order.
      start_time - The start time of the order in `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` format.
      end_time - The end time of the order in `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` format.
      delivery_type - The type of delivery for the order (e.g., "Delivery" or "Pickup").
      req_time - The required time for the order.
      dishes - A list of Dish objects representing the dishes included in the order.
      Returns:
      true if the order was placed successfully and all dishes were added; false otherwise.
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs.

    • getOrdersForRestaurant

      public List<Order> getOrdersForRestaurant(int userId)
      Retrieves a list of orders associated with the restaurant where the specified user works.

      This method queries the database to fetch all orders placed at the restaurant that the user (identified by the provided user ID) is associated with. The method joins the `orders`, `order_items`, and `dishes` tables to gather order details, including the status of each order and the list of dishes associated with it. The dishes are represented as a concatenated string with remarks.

      Parameters:
      userId - The ID of the user whose associated restaurant's orders are to be retrieved.
      Returns:
      A list of Order objects representing the orders for the restaurant associated with the user.

    • addDishToMenuTable

      public boolean addDishToMenuTable(int restId)
      Adds the latest dish to the menu of a specified restaurant.

      This method inserts a new entry into the `menu` table by selecting the maximum dish ID from the `dishes` table and associating it with the given restaurant ID. The assumption is that the dish with the highest ID is the most recently added dish.

      Parameters:
      restId - The ID of the restaurant to which the latest dish should be added.
      Returns:
      true if the dish was successfully added to the menu; false otherwise.

    • getRestaurantForWorker

      public Restaurant getRestaurantForWorker(int userId)
      Retrieves the restaurant associated with a specific worker based on their user ID.

      This method queries the database to find the restaurant where the worker is employed. The worker is identified by the provided user ID, and the method returns the corresponding restaurant details.

      Parameters:
      userId - The ID of the user (worker) whose associated restaurant is to be retrieved.
      Returns:
      A Restaurant object containing the restaurant details (ID, name, address, branch) if found, or null if no matching restaurant is found or if an error occurs.

    • addCustomerToDB

      public boolean addCustomerToDB(String id, String firstName, String lastName, String email, String address, String username, String password, String phoneNumber, double credits, String homeBranch, String userType)
      Adds a new customer to the database with the provided details.

      This method inserts a new record into the `users` table with the given customer information. It returns a boolean indicating whether the operation was successful.

      Parameters:
      id - The unique identifier for the customer.
      firstName - The first name of the customer.
      lastName - The last name of the customer.
      email - The email address of the customer.
      address - The physical address of the customer.
      username - The username chosen by the customer.
      password - The password chosen by the customer.

      credits - The initial amount of credits the customer has.
      homeBranch - The home branch associated with the customer.
      userType - The type of user (e.g., customer, admin).
      Returns:
      true if the customer was successfully added to the database; false otherwise.

    • getUserByUsernameAndPassword

      public User getUserByUsernameAndPassword(String username, String password)
      Retrieves a user from the database based on the provided username and password.

      This method queries the `users` table to find a user that matches the given username and password. If a matching user is found, a `User` object is populated with the user's details and returned. If no match is found, the method returns null.

      Parameters:
      username - The username of the user to be retrieved.
      password - The password of the user to be retrieved.
      Returns:
      A User object containing the user's details if found; null if no user is found with the given credentials.

    • getAllRestaurants

      public List<Restaurant> getAllRestaurants()
      Retrieves a list of all restaurants from the database.

      This method queries the `restaurants` table to retrieve all restaurant records. Each record is mapped to a `Restaurant` object and added to a list, which is then returned.

      Returns:
      A list of Restaurant objects representing all the restaurants in the database. The list will be empty if there are no restaurants or if an error occurs during the query.

    • getDishesByRestaurantId

      public List<Dish> getDishesByRestaurantId(int restaurantId)
      Retrieves a list of dishes offered by a specific restaurant.

      This method queries the database to fetch all dishes associated with a given restaurant ID. The method joins the `dishes`, `menu`, and `restaurants` tables to filter dishes based on the restaurant ID provided. Each dish is mapped to a Dish object and added to a list, which is then returned.

      Parameters:
      restaurantId - The ID of the restaurant whose dishes are to be retrieved.
      Returns:
      A list of Dish objects representing the dishes offered by the specified restaurant. The list will be empty if no dishes are found or if an error occurs during the query.

    • getDishesForUser

      public List<Dish> getDishesForUser(int userId) throws SQLException
      Retrieves a list of dishes available for a specific user based on their associated restaurant.

      This method queries the database to fetch all dishes that are available in the restaurant where the user, identified by their user ID, is employed. The method joins the `dishes`, `menu`, and `worker` tables to filter dishes based on the restaurant associated with the user. Each dish is mapped to a Dish object and added to a list, which is then returned.

      Parameters:
      userId - The ID of the user whose associated restaurant's dishes are to be retrieved.
      Returns:
      A list of Dish objects representing the dishes available for the user. The list will be empty if no dishes are found.
      Throws:
      SQLException - If a database access error occurs.

    • DeleteDishByDishId

      public boolean DeleteDishByDishId(int dishId)
      Deletes a dish from the database, including its entries in both the `menu` and `dishes` tables.

      This method performs a transactional delete operation, first removing the dish from the `menu` table and then from the `dishes` table. If any step fails, the transaction is rolled back to ensure data consistency.

      Parameters:
      dishId - The ID of the dish to be deleted.
      Returns:
      true if the dish was successfully deleted from both tables; false otherwise.

    • addDishToDB

      public boolean addDishToDB(Dish dish)
      Adds a new dish to the `dishes` table in the database.

      This method inserts a dish into the `dishes` table with the specified name, type, size, and price. The dish details are provided through the Dish object passed as a parameter.

      Parameters:
      dish - The Dish object containing the details of the dish to be added.
      Returns:
      true if the dish was successfully added to the database; false otherwise.

    • EditDishInDB

      public boolean EditDishInDB(Dish dish)
      Updates an existing dish in the `dishes` table in the database.

      This method updates the details of a dish in the `dishes` table based on the dish ID provided in the Dish object. The dish's name, type, size, and price are updated in the database.

      Parameters:
      dish - The Dish object containing the updated details of the dish, including its ID.

      true if the dish was successfully updated in the database; false otherwise.

    • getRestaurantsByBranch

      public List<Restaurant> getRestaurantsByBranch(String Manager_branch)
      Retrieves a list of restaurants that belong to a specific branch.

      This method queries the `restaurants` table in the database to fetch all restaurants that belong to the specified branch. The method returns a list of Restaurant objects, each representing a restaurant in the specified branch.

    • calculateIncomeByDate

      public Double calculateIncomeByDate(int res_id, LocalDate first_date, LocalDate last_date) throws SQLException
      Calculates the total income generated by a specific restaurant within a given date range.

      This method executes a query on the `orders` table to sum up the total prices of all orders placed at a specified restaurant within the provided date range. If no orders match the criteria, the method returns 0.0.

      Parameters:
      res_id - The ID of the restaurant for which the income is being calculated.
      first_date - The start date of the date range.
      last_date - The end date of the date range.
      Returns:
      The total income generated by the restaurant within the specified date range, or 0.0 if no matching records are found.
      Throws:
      SQLException - If a database access error occurs.

    • getDishOrderCounts

      public List<String> getDishOrderCounts(int restaurantId, LocalDate startDate, LocalDate endDate) throws SQLException
      Retrieves the count of orders for each dish in a specific restaurant within a given date range.

      This method executes a query to find out how many times each dish was ordered at a specified restaurant within the provided date range. The results are returned as a list of strings, where each string contains the dish name and the number of times it was ordered.

      Parameters:
      restaurantId - The ID of the restaurant for which the dish order counts are being retrieved.
      startDate - The start date of the date range.
      endDate - The end date of the date range.
      Returns:
      A list of strings, each containing the dish name and the number of times it was ordered, sorted in descending order by the number of times ordered.
      Throws:
      SQLException - If a database access error occurs.

    • getLateOrderStats

      public int[] getLateOrderStats(int restaurantId, LocalDate startDate, LocalDate endDate) throws SQLException
      Retrieves statistics on late orders for a specific restaurant within a given date range.

      This method executes a query to count the number of late orders and the total number of orders for a specified restaurant within the provided date range. The results are returned as an array of integers, where the first element represents the count of late orders and the second element represents the total number of orders.

      Parameters:
      restaurantId - The ID of the restaurant for which the late order statistics are being retrieved.
      startDate - The start date of the date range.
      endDate - The end date of the date range.
      Returns:
      An array of integers, where the first element is the count of late orders and the second element is the total number of orders.
      Throws:
      SQLException - If a database access error occurs.

    • getQuarterlyOrderStats

      public Map<String,int[]> getQuarterlyOrderStats(LocalDate startDate, LocalDate endDate) throws SQLException
      Retrieves quarterly order statistics for a specified date range.

      This method queries the database to count the number of orders and calculate the total revenue for each day within the specified date range. The results are stored in a map where the key is the date (as a string) and the value is an array of integers, where the first element represents the number of orders on that day and the second element represents the total revenue for that day.

      Parameters:
      startDate - The start date of the date range.
      endDate - The end date of the date range.
      Returns:
      A map where the key is the date (in "yyyy-MM-dd" format) and the value is an array of integers. The first element of the array represents the number of orders on that day, and the second element represents the total revenue for that day.
      Throws:
      SQLException - If a database access error occurs.
